content: This medication is not a substitute for personalized medical advice. Always consult your healthcare provider for comprehensive information about this product and your specific health needs. Ondansetron, commonly sold under brand names such as Zuplenz, is used to prevent nausea and vomiting caused by cancer treatments like chemotherapy and radiation therapy, as well as medications used for anesthesia before surgery. It can be used alone or in combination with other medications. Before using ondansetron oral soluble film, read the patient information leaflet and instructions provided by your pharmacist. This medication is designed to dissolve on the tongue. Do not chew or swallow the film whole. With dry hands, open the protective foil pouch just before use. Remove one film and place it on your tongue, allowing it to dissolve completely (usually within 4 to 20 seconds). You can then swallow it with saliva or liquid, though liquid is not necessary. If your prescribed dose requires more than one film, let each film dissolve completely before taking the next one. To prevent nausea from chemotherapy, take this medication as directed by your doctor, typically 30 minutes before treatment begins. For nausea prevention from radiation therapy, take it 1 to 2 hours before the start of treatment. Follow your doctor’s instructions carefully. Ondansetron may be taken up to three times a day for 1 to 2 days after each chemotherapy or radiation session. If you are on a prescribed schedule, take it regularly to maximize its benefits. Dosage is based on your medical condition and response to treatment. For children, dosage may also depend on age and weight. Take this medication exactly as prescribed. Common side effects include headache, lightheadedness, dizziness, drowsiness, fatigue, and constipation. Remember, this medication has been prescribed because your doctor has determined that the benefits outweigh the risks of side effects. Rarely, ondansetron may increase serotonin levels and lead to a serious condition called serotonin syndrome or toxicity. The risk is higher if you are taking other drugs that increase serotonin levels. Inform your doctor or pharmacist about all medications you are taking to avoid potential interactions. Serious allergic reactions to this drug are rare. However, this is not a complete list of possible side effects. In the U.S., contact your doctor for medical advice about side effects. In Canada, consult your doctor for similar concerns. Before taking ondansetron, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it or have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other issues. Ondansetron may cause a condition affecting heart rhythm (QT prolongation). The risk of QT prolongation may increase if you have certain medical conditions or are taking other drugs that can cause QT prolongation. Low levels of potassium or magnesium in the blood can also increase this risk, especially if you are using certain medications (e.g., diuretics) or have conditions such as severe sweating, diarrhea, or vomiting. This drug may cause dizziness or drowsiness. Alcohol or marijuana (cannabis) can exacerbate these effects. Avoid driving, operating machinery, or performing tasks requiring alertness until you can do so safely. Refrain from consuming alcoholic beverages. During pregnancy, this medication should only be used when clearly needed, as it may harm an unborn baby. It is unknown if this drug passes into breast milk. Consult your doctor before breastfeeding. Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase the risk of serious side effects. Keep a list of all the products you use (including prescription, non-prescription, and herbal products) and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. The risk of serotonin syndrome/toxicity increases if you are taking other drugs that increase serotonin levels, such as MDMA (ecstasy), St. John’s wort, or certain antidepressants (e.g., SSRIs like fluoxetine or paroxetine, SNRIs like duloxetine or venlafaxine). In case of overdose, if someone has severe symptoms such as passing out or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222. While taking this medication, lab and/or medical tests (e.g., EKG) may be required. Keep all medical and lab appointments. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember unless it is near the time for your next dose. In that case, skip the missed dose and resume your regular schedule. Do not double the dose to catch up. Store this medication at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. This information is a summary and does not contain all possible details about this product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. Always consult your healthcare provider for complete information about this medication and your specific health needs.
